title: Skill rewrite for getting started, building a roadmap, planning and implementing
lead: The slicer skill (`ai.skill_text()`, committed as `skills/slicer/SKILL.md`) opens by routing the four jobs an agent arrives with: getting started, building a roadmap from the docs, planning or filing, and implementing. Its description names them, so the harness loads it for those requests.
findings_note: owner request 2026-11-02 (release 1.18.0, helping an agent get started): decision 3, update the slicer skill so it is the most useful for getting started, building a roadmap from docs, planning and implementing (split from `ai hooks`, which is its own slice)
boundary: **Not in this slice:** `ai hooks` (the next slice), prompt overrides, changes to the implement loop, the exit codes or the TRACKING block wording beyond what the routing needs, and Codex or Grok specific skill text.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Owner request 2026-11-02, decision 3: update the slicer skill so it is the most useful for getting started, building a roadmap from docs, planning and implementing. This slice is the skill half; the owner allowed splitting `ai hooks` out when the combined slice would exceed M, and it would (skill text, a settings merge and a guard command).

Today (`ai.skill_text`, ai.py ~1321-1347) the skill is the implement loop, the spec-gap rule, the exit codes, the TRACKING block, a closer, a relay sentence and a last line pointing at `slicer ai instructions --rest`. `SKILL_DESCRIPTION` (ai.py ~61) says "review a roadmap, plan work, take a slice, implement the next slice, or drive slicer". An agent asked to get started or to build a roadmap from docs gets the implement loop first, which is the wrong first step for both.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/ai.py`:
  - `SKILL_DESCRIPTION`: name the jobs. Proposed: "Drive a slicer roadmap. Use when asked to get started with slicer, build a roadmap from a project's docs, review a roadmap, plan work, take a slice, implement the next slice, or drive slicer. Read and change roadmap state only through slicer commands, never by opening .slicer/ files."
  - New `SKILL_JOBS` block placed after `TRACKING_RULE` and before the loop in `skill_text`. Proposed:

    ```text
    Pick the job you were asked to do:

    - Getting started in this project: run `slicer ai getting-started` and follow it.
    - Building a roadmap from the project's docs: run `slicer ai build-roadmap` and follow it.
    - Planning, filing, claims and review: run `slicer ai instructions --rest`.
    - Implementing a slice: follow the steps below.
    - A slice relay: run `slicer ai relay` (see the end of this skill).
    ```
  - `skill_text` keeps `LOOP`/`loop_text`, `handoff_policy_text`, `SPEC_GAP`, `EXITS`, `TRACKING`, the closer, the relay sentence and the last line exactly as they are, so `test_Skill_LastLine_PointsAtRest`, `test_Tracking_RequiresTheCliForReadsAndEdits_InInstructionsAndSkill` and the handoff tests keep passing.
- `skills/slicer/SKILL.md`, `.claude/skills/slicer/SKILL.md`, `.agents/skills/slicer/SKILL.md`: regenerated from `skill_text()` (the committed generic `done` text).
- `tests/test_ai.py`: new tests below.
- `docs/agents.md`: the `slicer ai skill` paragraph says the skill opens by routing the four jobs to `ai getting-started`, `ai build-roadmap`, `ai instructions --rest` and the loop.
- `CHANGELOG.md` `## [Unreleased]` `### Changed`: one entry.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
In `tests/test_ai.py`:

- `test_Skill_Description_NamesGettingStartedAndBuildingARoadmap`: `SKILL_DESCRIPTION` contains "get started" and "build a roadmap" and still "review a roadmap" and "plan work".
- `test_Skill_Jobs_RouteEachJobToItsCommand`: `skill_text()` contains `ai.SKILL_JOBS` before `ai.LOOP`, and `SKILL_JOBS` names `slicer ai getting-started`, `slicer ai build-roadmap`, `slicer ai instructions --rest` and `slicer ai relay`.
- `test_Skill_Jobs_InEveryFinishMode`: `skill_text("handoff")` and `skill_text("done", "report")` contain `SKILL_JOBS`.
- Existing tests that must stay green unchanged: `test_Skill_MatchesTheInstructionsLoop_AndTheCommittedFile` (no `import --skeleton` in the skill itself), `test_CommittedSkill_MatchesSkillText`, `test_Instructions_LeaveRenderUnread_AndDoNotLinkTheLongReference` (the skill stays under half of docs/agents.md), `test_Instructions_CommandExamples_AreAcceptedByTheParser`, `test_Instructions_Rest_LeavesOutEverySkillBlock` (`rest_text` must not gain `SKILL_JOBS`; add `SKILL_JOBS` to that test's block list).

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Add `SKILL_JOBS`, reword `SKILL_DESCRIPTION`, insert the block in `skill_text`.
2. Regenerate the three committed copies byte for byte from `skill_text()` (`slicer ai skill --output PATH --force` from the worktree's code, or `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m slicer ai skill > PATH`).
3. Update docs/agents.md and CHANGELOG.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- [ ] The skill opens with the job routing, and its description names getting started and building a roadmap.
- [ ] The loop, exit codes, TRACKING block, closer, relay sentence and last line are unchanged.
- [ ] `skills/slicer/SKILL.md`, `.claude/skills/slicer/SKILL.md` and `.agents/skills/slicer/SKILL.md` equal `slicer ai skill` output.
- [ ] Every `slicer` command in the skill parses; the skill stays under half of docs/agents.md.
- [ ] `python3 tests/affected.py --run`, the full suite, `slicer check` and `git diff --check` pass.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: Commit on the worktree branch; merging, pushing and publishing wait for the owner.
